object_description: flat angular solitaire between the two existing school buildings with a large footprint
geometry_property: set slightly back at the break area
sports hall one level below grade
design_condition: the flat angular volume is placed between the two existing school buildings along the rear building line, set slightly back at the central break area so that a forecourt with an entrance area is formed

positive: The height of the volume essentially fits well into the existing situation
The slightly set-back position creates an appropriate forecourt with an entrance area
By clearly addressing all school buildings the natural stone forecourt forms the functional and spatial focus
A new introverted outdoor space is created adjacent to the student garden
The open space at the street entrance is used for an all-weather pitch
The front garden is repaired in the spirit of a monument preservation reconstruction and adequately upgraded
The mezzanine houses the school kitchen and the library as the heart of the school
The library has an attractive connection to the playground
On the top floor all secondary school classrooms are combined in an interesting learning landscape
A glazed learning atrium illuminates and zones the central access area
Deep classrooms are additionally illuminated via internal skylight strips
The organisation of the underground sports hall floor with adjoining rooms is compact
Setting the hall back only one floor into the terrain avoids expensive excavation pit connections
Thanks to the compactness the target costs are met and economic realisation is likely
A consistently presented contribution with great potential in the floor plan layout of the school floor
negative: The formerly free contiguous outdoor space is divided into two areas by the position of the building
The external clarity is weakened by the additional ball court placed on the playing field
The uniform fibreglass concrete facade refuses to engage in dialogue between the two historic buildings
The contribution is not articulated in a sufficiently differentiated manner in this historical context
The spatial and structural logic of the entrance hall with gallery, shaft, lift and narrow staircase is unsatisfactory
The communication corridors are too narrow and reveal no spatial intention
Some usable areas are clearly undercut compared to the space programme
The requirements of ecological sustainability were barely adhered to
The presence of the sports hall on almost all sides at ground floor is a weak point
The uniform architectural expression is not convincing in the context of the two protected buildings
